questions.q: What does the lesson say is the main layer a Developer interview adds on top of what an Administrator interview covers?
options: A credit check
A physical fitness test
Nothing -- the two interviews are identical
Code -- a live coding exercise, a take-home, or a code-review exercise
questions.explain: The lesson states Developer interviews add code-focused exercises on top of the same behavioral questions every role gets.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say governor limits exist at all?
options: Because Salesforce is multi-tenant, and one org's badly-written code can't be allowed to degrade the platform for every other org
To make Apex harder to learn on purpose
Because Salesforce charges extra for higher limits
They exist only in sandbox orgs, not production
questions.explain: The lesson explains governor limits as a consequence of the multi-tenant architecture protecting shared infrastructure.

questions.q: Why does a non-bulkified trigger often pass a sandbox test but fail in production?
options: Production orgs run a different version of Apex
Triggers are disabled by default in sandboxes
Sandbox tests typically run with one record, while production can hand the trigger up to 200 records at once, exposing per-record queries or DML inside a loop
Governor limits don't apply in production
questions.explain: The lesson explains that bulkification issues only surface once a trigger processes many records at once, which a single-record sandbox test won't catch.

questions.q: What is the standard fix for trigger recursion described in the lesson?
options: Disabling the trigger entirely
A static boolean flag in a helper class, set on first entry and checked before the logic runs again in the same transaction
Increasing the governor limit for DML statements
Rewriting the trigger in a different programming language
questions.explain: The lesson describes the static-flag pattern as the standard way to prevent a trigger's own DML from re-triggering itself.

questions.q: What does the lesson recommend when discussing Lightning Web Components if your experience is limited to coursework?
options: State the limited experience plainly, and speak clearly about what you do understand -- components, events, and decorators
Claim deep production experience to sound more competitive
Avoid the topic entirely
Only discuss LWC if directly and explicitly asked
questions.explain: The lesson warns that overclaiming depth is more damaging than an honest, accurate account of what you've actually built.
